paragraphs: Here's what I want you to hold onto, friend. The people looked at the house they were building and it seemed like nothing next to the old one (Haggai 2:3). Maybe you know that feeling, when what you're building looks small and you wonder if it even counts. God doesn't wave that feeling away. He says, "Be strong…" and then, "Work! For I am with you, declares the LORD of Hosts." (Haggai 2:4)

Notice what He builds that courage on. He doesn't say the house is secretly fancier than it looks. He says He is with them, that His Spirit remains among them, and "do not be afraid." (Haggai 2:4-5) It's the same promise He made when they came out of Egypt, so it's not a new promise. It's an old one that's still standing.

And the house is His to fill. He says, "The silver is Mine, and the gold is Mine…" (Haggai 2:8) He promises to fill it with glory, that the latter glory will be greater than the former, and that in this place He will provide peace (Haggai 2:7-9). So when your work looks small, keep baking. The size of the thing was never what made it matter. The God who is with you is what makes it matter, and that's why my ovens stay ready.
